title: One allocation step
statement: Let $W$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $a\in\mathbb{N}$, and consider a setup configuration with arbitrary base configuration, input-head position, integer controller-head positions, and controller tapes. Suppose its phase is the allocation phase of direction $r\in\{\mathrm{right},\mathrm{left}\}$ indexed by $i\in\{0,1,2\}$, the unary tape reads a unit marker at its head, and the guide tape reads the origin marker at its head if and only if that head is at cell $0$. One step advances the allocation index to $i+1\pmod 3$, moves the unary head right by one exactly when $i=2$, moves the guide head one cell in direction $r$, and writes the origin marker at the guide cell previously under its head if that cell is $0$, writing an interior marker otherwise; all other tape contents and configuration data are unchanged.
hypotheses_covered: $W$ is a finite Turing machine over Booleans
a base configuration, input-head position, and integer controller-head positions
allocation direction is right or left and index is in $\{0,1,2\}$
unary tape reads a unit marker at its head
guide reads the origin marker exactly when its head is at $0$
replaced:
Consider a setup configuration in layout phase $i \in \{0,1,2\}$ of either direction,
and suppose the unary tape reads a unit marker at the unary head and the guide tape
reads the origin mark at the guide head exactly when that head is at cell $0$.  Then
one step moves to layout phase $i+1 \bmod 3$, writes the guide mark at the guide head,
moves the guide head one cell in the chosen direction, and advances the unary head by
one exactly when $i = 2$; everything else is unchanged.  Thus the controller spends
three guide cells per unary marker.
